messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] allele coding in a 'wild' family
messages.body_plain:
You need to first infer phase/haplotypes and then figure out, for each possible observed offspring genotype, what  true genotypes correspond, and then look at the codes in the help file for read.cross, described in the section "Value".

For a marker like ABxAC, we'd have four possible offspring genotypes, and the codes to assign to them would depend on phase in the parents

         ABxAC   ABxCA   BAxAC   BAxCA    <- parents' phase
   AA      1       3       2       4
   AB      2       4       1       3
   AC      3       1       4       2
   BC      4       2       3       1

For a marker like AAxAB, there are two possible offspring genotypes

         AAxAB   AAxBA   ABxAA   BAxAA    <- parents' phase
   AA      7       8       5       6
   AB      8       7       6       5

karl

messages.subject: Re: No get.ests()? + Heritability
messages.body_plain:
As for heritability, you may be able to calculate H2 directly if you have replication (e.g. multiple clones for each genotype).
You can also calculate [pseudo]H2 indirectly using a model of polygenic inheritance, which leverages relatedness among individuals. This has been implemented in qtlTools::polygenicQTL ... this function should be stable, but is still undergoing testing. I think R/qtl2 also has some of this functionality.

For example:
> library(devtools)
> install_github("jtlovell/qtlTools")
> library(qtlTools)
> library(rrBLUP)
> data(fake.f2)
> fake.f2<-calc.genoprob(fake.f2, step = 2, stepwidth = "fixed")
> polygenicQTL(cross = fake.f2, pheno.col = 1)

John

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] lod score from mqmscan
messages.body_plain:
The result of mqmscan(), if you use multiple phenotype columns, is a list of  data frames.

To get the peak LOD scores on each chromosome for the first trait, you could use

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Combining different groups into one
messages.body_plain:
You can try using the function movemarker() to move markers from one linkage group to another.

For example, with the hyper dataset, to paste all of the markers on chromosome 12 onto the end of chromosome 11, you could do:

  data(hyper)
  c12markers <- markernames(hyper, chr=12)
  for(marker in c12markers) {
      hyper <- movemarker(hyper, marker, 11)
  }

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Combining different groups into one
messages.body_plain:
Try reducing min.lod and increasing max.rf.

The main thing I'd focus on is figuring out why the markers are breaking up into three groups. To start, I'd look at tables of two-locus genotypes for marker pairs that are close by physically but are getting put into different linkage groups. Also I'd look at the plot.rf() image, with markers ordered by their physical location.

karl

Regarding the error message, we need to see exactly what code you used, preferably with example data, in order to diagnose the problem.

karl
